classification.reason: The coach provides a two-part actionable exercise to fix the racket flip: creating exaggerated lateral space from the ball and deliberately throwing the hand out to the side.

problem.title_as_question: Why Doesn't Your Racket Flip on the Forehand?
problem.definition: The forehand racket fails to flip or lag explosively because the forward swing is initiated straight toward the ball with the hand staying still, rather than pressing the hand outward to flip the racket around its center of mass.

symptoms.description: The racket does not flip or lags significantly slower into the slot at the start of the forward swing.
The forward swing feels tight, dead, and lacks effortless release or explosive wrist power.
Forehand quality degrades dramatically when standing stationary or moving inside-out compared to running wide.

causes.statement: The player initiates the forward swing vector straight toward the ball instead of laterally out to their side.
The player attempts to flip the racket tip back while holding the hand still or pivoting around the butt cap rather than moving hand and head in equal and opposite directions.
The player sets up too close to the ball, so the brain inhibits throwing the hand outward because doing so would cause a complete miss.
Moving inside-out or to the left forces the player to fight against the body's momentum, collapsing the hand inward unless actively pressed out.

angles.summary: Pressing the hand outward while the racket head moves back spins the racket around its center of mass, doubling its flip speed.
Jannik Sinner, Roger Federer, and Jack Sock all display an aggressive outward hand path to the right before driving forward through contact.
Jack Sock's casual flick illustrates a slow flip pivoting only around the hand/butt cap without an outward hand press.

solutions.summary: Set up with exaggerated lateral left-to-right space between your body and the incoming ball.
solutions.external_goal: Leave way more space in the left to right direction than you think you need.

solutions.summary: At the start of the forward swing, deliberately throw your hitting hand out to the right before driving toward the opponent.
solutions.external_goal: Throw the hand out to the right very quickly at the forward swing transition.

solutions.summary: Use an early kinesthetic cue to press the racket and hand outward before the swing to ensure the outward path is not forgotten.
solutions.external_goal: Press the racket and hand out early to the right side.
